來源顯示，水鍵口琴（玻璃琴）可於宮廷演奏、公開音樂會、歌劇、芭蕾、電影配樂及獨奏: The source shows that the glass harmonica can be heard in court performance, public concerts, opera, ballet, film scores, and in solos, chamber music, electronic music and popular music. The works named are Mozart's K.617 and K.356, Beethoven's Leonore Prohaska, the accompaniment originally specified for Donizetti's Lucia di Lammermoor, the seventh and fourteenth movements of Saint-Saëns's The Carnival of the Animals, Richard Strauss's Die Frau ohne Schatten, the ballet Othello, and Benjamin's Written on Skin.
水鍵口琴屬體鳴樂器，發聲來自濕潤手指摩擦玻璃碗或杯緣。其音色接近長笛，可拉長成持: The glass harmonica is an idiophone whose sound comes from wet fingers rubbing the rims of glass bowls or goblets. Its timbre is close to the flute, and notes can be drawn out into a continuous sound. Volume and dynamics are controlled by the pressure of the fingertips: more pressure gives more volume, less gives less. Franklin's version arranges thirty-seven glass bowls horizontally, covers three octaves with semitones, and can sound ten notes at once, unlike the upright goblet form, where several notes are hard to play together. Most of its pitches fall between about one thousand and four thousand hertz, so listeners find it hard to tell where the sound comes from.
水鍵口琴是玻璃琴的別名之一。摩擦玻璃杯發聲的現象可追溯至文藝復興，伽利略與 At: Water-key harmonica is one of the alternative names for the glass harmonica. The phenomenon of sounding a glass by friction goes back to the Renaissance, and Galileo and Athanasius Kircher studied it. In the 1740s Pockrich played on goblets filled with water in London; Delavaux improved the idea, and Gluck also performed on a similar instrument. In 1761 Benjamin Franklin, inspired by Delavaux, made with Charles James an instrument of horizontal glass bowls turned by a pedal, first performed by Marianne Davies in 1762. The instrument reached the courts of England, Italy and the Holy Roman Empire, and in 1764 it reached Philadelphia; it declined after 1820, was revived in the twentieth century by Hoffmann, was modified by Finkenbeiner, and the Baschet brothers made a separate crystal organ.
水鍵口琴是玻璃琴的別名，屬摩擦體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號: Water-key harmonica is another name for the glass harmonica, a friction idiophone, Hornbostel-Sachs number 133.2. It sounds with a series of glass bowls or goblets of graduated size, and the player rubs the rims with wet fingers, the friction producing the pitch. Franklin's design mounts the bowls horizontally on an iron spindle turned by a pedal, so that several can be touched at once. The instrument was played in England, Italy and at courts, and composers used it in opera, ballet and modern recordings.

演奏者不需手持樂器，而是坐在富蘭克林式玻璃琴前，以腳踩踏板使水平鐵軸旋轉，再用沾: The player does not hold the instrument but sits in front of a Franklin-style glass harmonica, works the pedal with the foot to spin the horizontal iron spindle, and touches the rims of the glass bowls with wet fingers to make them sound. A beginner can first tell the pitch by the colour of the bowl rim, and control the volume and the duration with the pressure of the fingertips; if the water is on the acid side, a little chalk dust on the fingers helps the sound come clear. The basic order is to wet the fingers, start the pedal, rub the rims with the fingertips, and practise touching several bowls at once to produce harmony.
發聲體為玻璃或水晶製成的碗、杯，依尺寸排列；富蘭克林式將三十七個玻璃碗水平穿於鐵: The sounding body is bowls or goblets of glass or crystal, arranged by size; the Franklin design threads thirty-seven glass bowls horizontally on an iron spindle turned by a pedal, the rims tinted different colours, and they are rubbed with wet fingers, with chalk dust allowed. Later copies use clear glass, ordinary glass and pure quartz glass, with gold stripes added. Other modern versions are built from metal resonating rods, glass rods, metal handles and metal blocks, with glass fibre or a metal case, wooden blocks and metal wire helping the resonance.
